title: N-Doped Mesoporous Carbon Film with Pinned Carbon Nanotube as Free-Standing Anode for Fast-Charging Li-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract A N-doped mesoporous carbon film with a pinned carbon nanotube was prepared by a hydrothermal soft-template self-assembly and metal-catalyzed graphitization approach, using phenolic resin/dicyandiamide as the solid carbon and nitrogen sources and F127 micelles as a mesoporous template. The thickness of the mesoporous carbon membrane was determined by the polymerization degree of phenolic resin and was adjustable by tuning the reagent concentration in the hydrothermal reaction. These NMCF-NCNT films show a high graphitization degree, large specific surface area, rich nitrogen dopant, and high mechanical strength. Importantly, the NCNT grown on the mesoporous carbon film constructs a conductive pathway between the carbon film and coin cell, and the mesopores in NMCF accelerate the electrolyte diffusion when NMCF-NCNT films are applied as free-standing anodes in LiBs. The NMCF-NCNT-1 with a thickness of 1 μm delivered the optimum electrochemical properties of 750 mAh g–1 at 0.1 A g–1, 578 mAh g–1 at 5 A g–1 after 30 cycles, and 661 mAh g–1 at 1 A g–1 after 600 cycles. Such good electrochemical performance could be attributed to the thinnest NMCF-NCNT-1 membrane granting high electrical conductivity, fast Li+ diffusion, and preeminent structural stabilization. This work aims at the preparation of a self-supporting-structured mesoporous carbon film with pinned carbon nanotube, the regulation of micro-nanostructure, and the optimization of electrochemical performance, which may gain a new insight into the design of free-standing carbon membrane electrodes for fast-charging LiBs.

title: Reorganization of Interfacial Water by Cu–Ru Interfaces for Efficient Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction offers a sustainable route for ammonia (NH3) synthesis, yet its efficiency is limited by sluggish N–O bond cleavage, incomplete NOx hydrogenation, and competing hydrogen evolution reaction. However, how catalyst structural engineering regulates the interfacial microenvironment remains unclear, despite its critical importance for constructing efficient catalysts. Here, we report a Cu3Ru7 catalyst with abundant Cu–Ru interfaces, where interface-induced water reorganization enables efficient NH3 production. The Cu3Ru7 catalyst exhibits an impressive NH3 formation rate of 19.7 mmol h–1 cm–2 at 5 A cm–2 in a membrane electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzer and remains stable at 2 A cm–2 with an NH3 Faradaic efficiency of ∼86% for 500 h. A scale-up demonstration using a 100 cm2 MEA electrolyzer affords an NH3 formation rate up to 1.5 mol h–1 at 400 A. The in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) reveals that Cu3Ru7 catalyst establishes a moderate interfacial hydrogen-bond network, which creates a water-mediated interfacial micro environment that facilitates NOx deoxygenation and subsequent NHx formation. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations further reveal that the Cu–Ru interface stabilizes the dissociating oxygen atom through a persistent and dynamically connected hydrogen-bond network, thereby facilitating sequential NO3– → NO2 → NO conversion. Meanwhile, the surrounding Cu matrix attenuates the excessive *H accumulation characteristic of Ru, suppressing the hydrogen evolution reaction. This work establishes Cu–Ru interface-induced interfacial water reorganization as a strategy for improving electrocatalytic nitrate reduction performance.

title: Amino‐Site Directed Molecular Engineering Enables Novel Wide‐Bandgap Organic Crystal With Record‐Breaking High Birefringence
abstract: ABSTRACT Birefringent crystals are vital functional materials for light‐polarization modulation, widely utilized in optical communications, laser technology, displays, imaging, and photodetection. High‐performance birefringent crystals require broad optical band gaps to realize wide visible‐to‐ultraviolet transparency. However, large birefringence and wide band gap are difficult to achieve simultaneously, since highly polarizable structural units easily induce low‐energy electronic transitions. Herein, an amino‐position regulation strategy is proposed via proton‐transfer‐driven self‐assembly of 2‐, 3‐, and 4‐aminopyridines with 4, 5‐dicyanoimidazole, integrating prominent polarizability anisotropy and large molecular HOMO–LUMO gaps. Three organic crystals, [(C 5 N 2 H 7 ) + (C 5 N 4 H) − ]·H 2 O (2AP‐DCI‐W), [(C 5 N 2 H 7 ) + (C 5 N 4 H 2 )(C 5 N 4 H) − ] [3AP‐(DCI) 2 ], and [(C 5 N 2 H 7 ) + (C 5 N 4 H) − ] (4AP‐DCI), were successfully synthesized. Amino‐substitution position modulates the electrostatic distribution, intermolecular interactions, and packing modes of π‐conjugated units, progressively improving both birefringence and optical band gap. 4AP‐DCI exhibits the optimal overall performance with a calculated birefringence of 0.514 at 546 nm and a broad band gap of 4.06 eV. To our knowledge, this value represents the highest birefringence among all organic birefringent crystals with band gaps over 4.0 eV. This work provides an effective molecular strategy to balance large birefringence and broad transparency by tuning the position and spatial arrangement of organic π‐conjugated functional units.

title: Self‐Assembly and Humidity‐Adaptive Memristive Behavior of Benzophosphole Nanohoops
abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling the condensed‐state properties of π‐conjugated macrocycles via molecular structure remains a fundamental challenge in supramolecular chemistry. Here, we report benzophosphole‐embedded nanohoops as a heteroatom‐doped platform where spatial configuration ( exo vs. endo ) directly governs molecular conformation, self‐assembly, and electronic function. The endo ‐nanohoop adopts a unique outward‐facing conformer that assembles into discrete tetrameric cage‐like assemblies stabilized by cooperative P═O···H 2 O interactions, which further evolve into hierarchical hollow nanobowl architectures exhibiting aggregation‐induced emission enhancement (AIEE). This differentiation generates distinct hydration microenvironments that correlate with divergent memristive behaviors. The exo ‐analogues exhibit highly uniform volatile threshold switching arising from transient ion migration dynamics, enabling physical reservoir computing. In contrast, the endo ‐framework possesses a distinct hydration microenvironment and exhibits robust analog non‐volatile memory behavior. Available evidence suggests a possible mechanism in which water acts as structural nodes that bridge Ag clusters and coordinate ion transport with filament stability, thereby enabling non‐volatile memristive behavior. Leveraging the humidity‐dependent switching characteristics of the exo system, we further demonstrate a humidity‑sensitive resistive switching capable of real‐time and noise‐resistant respiratory monitoring. These findings establish a direct correlation between molecular structure, water confinement, and adaptive electronic functionality, providing a supramolecular strategy for designing intelligent organic memristive materials and sensing‐memory integrated hardware.

title: Single‐Step Orientational Self‐Assembly of Pd Metallacycles and Heterometallic Pd–Pt Helical Cages From Heteroditopic Ligands
abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling the self‐assembly of heterometallic supramolecular architectures without generating statistical mixtures remains a major challenge. Here, we show that adaptable coordination modes of tetrazole units in heterodipotic tetrazole–pyridine ligands direct both orientational self‐sorting and selective metal organization. Reaction with cis‐protected Pd(II) acceptors afforded Pd 6 ( L ) 4 metallacycles ( L = L1 – L3 ), in which tetrazolate coordination through an unusual (2,3) binding mode is exploited in the orientational self‐sorting. In contrast, ligand L4 employed its (1,3) coordination mode together with the pyridyl donors to generate a Pd 9 ( L4 ) 6 helical cage and the heterometallic Pd 9 Ag( L4 ) 6 , and Pd 3 Pt 6 ( L4 ) 6 cages in single‐step self‐assembly processes. Remarkably, despite the closely matched coordination preferences of Pd(II) and Pt(II), the synergistic effects of donor inequivalence and the flexible coordination behavior selectively partitions the two congeneric d 8 ions into distinct coordination sites within the Pd 3 Pt 6 ( L4 ) 6 cage. The uncommon (1,2,3) tetrazolate binding mode additionally enables formation of the Pd 9 Ag( L4 ) 6 cage. Encapsulation of enantiopure guests by the helical cages induces host chirality and corresponding chiroptical responses. These results demonstrate that coordination mode flexibility of the tetrazole moiety combined with the pyridyl unit can direct the formation of metallacycles and helical cages and enable selective partitioning of closely related metal ions in a single‐step assembly.

title: Site Sensitivity Resulting in Selective Hydroxylamine Electrosynthesis
abstract: Abstract The electroreduction of nitrogen oxides offers a promising route for green synthesis of hydroxylamine (NH2OH). Although Pd exhibited high selectivity toward NH2OH production experimentally, we found the dominant hollow sites of pristine Pd prefer ammonia production via the NOH*-pathway. This discrepancy was resolved by unveiling the critical roles of in situ hydriding of Pd under operando conditions. Using Grand Canonical Monte Carlo simulations driven by machine learning potential, we demonstrated the potential-dependent structural evolution from pristine Pd to palladium hydride (PdHx) under −0.11 to −0.51 V vs RHE. For the in situ-generated PdHx surfaces with some amorphous or disordering features, the dominant hollow sites of Pd are blocked by adsorbed H* species, thereby repelling NO* to adsorb obliquely on PdHx top sites. The adsorption configuration of NO* steers the reaction pathway from NOH* to HNO* formation, leading to NH2OH* production eventually. In addition, the PdHx top sites exhibit generally downshifted d-band centers, promoting NH2OH* desorption and preventing its over-reduction to ammonia. At last, a site sensitivity was proposed for hydroxylamine electrosynthesis based on the analysis on a variety of catalysts; the formation energies of HNO* vs NOH* and the adsorption energy of NH2OH* were identified as important features resulting in high hydroxylamine selectivity.

title: Solvent-Directed Supramolecular Reconstruction Through Coupled Coordination-Bond Dynamics and Covalent-Bond Formation
abstract: Abstract Understanding how external stimuli actively direct bond reorganization and supramolecular reconstruction remains a fundamental challenge in adaptive self-assembly. Although solvent-induced transformations are widely observed in supramolecular systems, the molecular mechanisms by which solvents simultaneously regulate coordination-bond dynamics and covalent-bond formation remain poorly understood. Herein, we report a rare cluster-based triply interlocked [2]catenane, [(Tp*WS3Cu3)8(L)12(OTf)8](OTf)8 ([1(OTf)8], Tp* = tris(3,5-dimethylpyrazolyl)borate; L = (Z)-4,4′-(but-1-en-3-yne-1,4-diyl)dipyridine; OTf– = trifluoromethanesulfonate), which undergoes methanol-directed supramolecular reconstruction into an octahedral cage. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction establishes the structures of both the interlocked precursor and the reconstructed product, while solution-state NMR spectroscopy and control experiments reveal a rapid and highly selective reconstruction process. Density functional theory calculations propose key intermediates and elucidate the dual mechanistic role of methanol during the reconstruction. Methanol promotes displacement of weakly coordinated triflate ligands and perturbs the local coordination environment, thereby initiating coordination-bond reorganization. Subsequent methanol coordination further recognizes the coordination framework and facilitates alkyne-sulfide addition that stabilizes the emerging octahedral architecture. The reconstruction therefore proceeds through coupled coordination-bond dynamics and covalent-bond formation rather than simple cage dissociation and reassembly. These findings provide a molecular-level mechanistic framework for understanding how solvent molecules can actively direct supramolecular reconstruction through the interplay of coordination chemistry and chemical reactivity.

title: Chemically Fueled Amplification of Supramolecular Asymmetry with Double Chiroptical Inversion
abstract: Abstract Amplification of asymmetry in supramolecular polymers is typically studied under equilibrium conditions in apolar solvents, while examples in aqueous media, under nonequilibrium conditions or under temporal chemical control remain scarce. Here we demonstrate chemically fueled amplification of supramolecular asymmetry in water using perylene diimide (PDI) derivatives. The chemically fueled reaction cycle uses sodium dithionite to reduce and depolymerize kinetically stable helical aggregates, while subsequent oxidation by dissolved oxygen restores them. This transient disassembly–reassembly process yields amplification of asymmetry in Majority Rules (MR) experiments that is absent in the kinetically trapped system. In Sergeants-and-Soldiers (SaS) experiments, the fueled cycle shows an unusual composition-dependent response characterized by a double chiroptical inversion as a function of sergeant fraction. A phase model captures the emergence of three composition regimes and rationalizes the observed CD response. Overall, we show how chemical fuels can regulate asymmetry amplification in aqueous supramolecular polymers and highlight the role of phase competition in complex chiral self-assembly.

title: Weak Solvation Engineering of Reduction‐Stable Electrolytes for Durable Continuous Lithium‐Mediated Ammonia Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Continuous lithium‐mediated nitrogen reduction reaction (Li‐NRR), which integrates anodic hydrogen oxidation with cathodic nitrogen fixation, opens a viable pathway for ambient ammonia synthesis. Nevertheless, its long‐term and efficient operation remains tremendously challenging due to severe solvent issues including polymerization, volatilization, and reductive decomposition. Here, we fundamentally uncover the intrinsic reductive decomposition mechanism of solvent molecules in ion–solvent complex‐dominated electrolytes, and develop a weak‐solvent modulation strategy to significantly enhance the reduction stability of solvent frameworks toward durable and efficient Li‐NRR operation. The optimized weakly solvating electrolyte attenuates solvent molecule distortion by Li + and promotes the formation of an anion‑enriched solvation sheath and a nanocrystalline LiF‑rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Such a functional SEI layer effectively suppresses solvent decomposition on the cathode and constructs a fast Li + transport network via abundant surface pathways and grain boundaries, which synergistically improves Li plating kinetics and nitrogen fixation efficiency, as well as stability. Benefiting from these optimizations, we achieve stable and continuous N 2 electroreduction over 300 h. Meanwhile, the system delivers a high NH 3 Faradaic efficiency of 69.5% and an improved energy efficiency up to 23.2%. This work provides an effective molecular design strategy that significantly enhances the energy efficiency and stability of Li‐NRR.

title: Overcoming Mass‐Transport Limitations in Electrocatalytic Dehalogenation via DMSO‐Engineered Hydrogen Bonds
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic conversion of water‐soluble organics in aqueous media offers a sustainable route to high‐value chemicals, yet sluggish mass transport remains a critical bottleneck at industrially relevant current densities. Here, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) is employed as the modifier to enhance mass transport by reconstructing hydrogen‐bond (H‐bond) networks. In the bulk electrolyte, DMSO inserts into the dense hydrogen bonds to expand the free‐volume distribution, releasing reactants from the solvation shell and accelerating their diffusion. Simultaneously, interfacial interactions between DMSO, reactants, and cations enrich local reactant concentrations, cooperatively facilitating the reaction kinetics. This dual‐enhancement mechanism achieves ∼60% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in electrocatalytic dehalogenative hydrogenolysis at 300 mA cm −2 . Our strategy demonstrates broad utility across the dehalogenative hydrogenation of other halogenated substrates and the hydrogenation of nitriles/nitro compounds, delivering >10% FE improvements. By coupling bulk diffusion acceleration with interfacial reactant enrichment, this work offers a promising strategy to overcome mass transport limitations in aqueous electrosynthesis.

title: CHARMM-Compatible Molecular Mechanics Force Fields for Multiscale Modeling of HIV-1 Replication Inhibitors
abstract: Abstract Molecular dynamics simulations provide insight into inhibitor-protein interactions and support rational drug design; however, their accuracy depends on reliable molecular mechanics force field parameters and coarse-grained representations that retain relevant molecular features. Although force field parameter sets for biomacromolecules are well established, the chemical diversity of small-molecule inhibitors often requires the development of system-specific parameters. Here, we present a parametrization framework integrating quantum mechanical optimization, experimental benchmarking, and small-molecule coarse-graining, demonstrated using HIV-1 inhibitors targeting multiple stages of the viral replication cycle. We provide a curated data set of CHARMM-compatible force field parameters for 12 HIV-1 inhibitors and the HIV assembly cofactor inositol hexakisphosphate (IP6), together with geometry-optimized atomic structures and ligand restraint files. The resulting parameters are validated against experimental structural and thermodynamic benchmarks, including lenacapavir binding free energy estimates, through inhibitor-bound complex simulations. We demonstrate applications of the parameter data set by quantifying inhibitor-protein interactions, including the free-energy profile of an integrase strand transfer inhibitor interacting with the viral capsid lattice, and the binding energetics of an allosteric integrase inhibitor. Furthermore, we extend the all-atom inhibitor parameter data set through a novel coarse-graining strategy for small molecules that preserves key electrostatic features. The HIV-1 inhibitor force field parameter data set is a publicly available resource that establishes a unified framework for multiscale modeling of HIV-1 inhibitors and facilitates computational and structural biology studies of drug resistance and inhibitor design. More generally, the framework presented here is broadly applicable to small-molecule parametrization and multiscale simulations in other therapeutic and biomolecular contexts.

title: Electrostatic Cation Intercalation Into Polymeric Self‐Assembled Monolayers Enables Ambient‐Air Fabrication of 32.73% Efficient Monolithic Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Polymeric self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) enable stable, efficient, and scalable perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (TSCs) based on silicon heterojunction (HJT) bottom cells. However, severe steric hindrance within the polymer matrix disrupts the directional anchoring of phosphonate groups, thereby limiting macroscopic work‐function regulation and sustaining a persistent hole‐extraction barrier. Herein, we report a targeted molecular reconstruction of the buried interface via the electrostatic intercalation of phenethylammonium iodide (PEAI). Templated by the polymer backbone, the intercalated PEA + cations adopt a highly directional vertical arrangement. This oriented molecular scaffold provides a strong intrinsic dipole while driving the electronegative iodide (I − ) counterions to enrich at the uppermost interface. This synergistic spatial decoupling maximizes the net upward dipole, triggering a favorable energy level realignment that effectively overcomes the hole extraction barrier. Concurrently, the halide‐enriched SAM dictates crystallization kinetics during ambient‐air slot‐die coating, inducing rapid “burst nucleation” to minimize solvate intermediates and suppress basal voids. Consequently, our 1 cm 2 TSC achieves an independently certified power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 32.73%. Benefiting from monolithic crystallographic integrity, the unencapsulated device maintains an enhanced T 80 lifetime of 2182 h under continuous maximum power point tracking.

title: Thermoresponsive Miktoarm Glycopolymer–Protein Conjugates Based on Molecular Recognition: Synthesis and Self-Assembly
abstract: Abstract Simultaneously modifying proteins with different polymers can enrich protein functions and provide various polymer–protein conjugates. Investigating the self-assembly of complex amphiphilic polymer–protein conjugates offers insights into the formation of different protein structures. Herein, we synthesize a new bifunctional chain transfer agent with both an adamantyl group and a biotin group (AB-CTA) to prepare the thermoresponsive poly(di(ethylene glycol) methyl ether methacrylate) with the two functional groups (AB-PDEGMA). Two types of glycopolymers were synthesized and each was modified with a β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) group. AB-PDEGMA was mixed with the β-CD-modified glycopolymer, affording a block copolymer. It was then conjugated to streptavidin (SA) to prepare miktoarm glycopolymer–protein conjugates. The whole process is modularized based on molecular recognition of adamantane/β-CD and SA/biotin. It is accessible to adjust the polymer type and chain length to prepare the desired conjugates. Self-assembly of the miktoarm glycopolymer-SA conjugates was investigated above their lower critical solution temperatures. Assemblies including spherical micelles, compound micelles with patchy structures, and proteinosomes could be obtained. The influences of the binding number of the block copolymer and PDEGMA chain length on self-assembly were revealed, which was consistent with conclusions reported in previous simulation articles.

title: From Accurate Quantum Chemistry to Converged Thermodynamics for Ion Pairing in Solution
abstract: Abstract Quantitative prediction of thermodynamic properties in solution is essential for translating atomistic simulations into reliable chemical insight. As an exemplar system, the behavior of CaCO3 in water has been widely studied to understand its mineralization in seawater, with potential implications for carbon-capture strategies. However, making accurate computational predictions has been a long-standing challenge, requiring both highly accurate electronic structure methods and extensive statistical sampling. Here, we combine advances in machine learning and electronic structure theory to fully resolve the ion pairing free energy of CaCO3 with explicit solvation. We show that achieving quantitative agreement with experiment requires going beyond density functional theory up to the “gold-standard” coupled cluster theory with single, double, and perturbative triple excitations [CCSD(T)]. We generate a set of systematically improvable models, enabling reliable insights into the initial association mechanism of Ca and CO3 ions prior to nucleation while fully quantifying enthalpic and entropic effects. These quantitatively accurate models further resolve a long-standing lack of consensus surrounding the hydration mechanism of the calcium ion in solution. Our results demonstrate that CCSD(T)-level thermodynamic predictions of complex aqueous systems can now be routinely achieved.

title: Unveiling π-Radical Induced Regioselective Pathways in On-Surface Synthesis of Kekulene-Hexaone
abstract: Abstract On-surface synthesized nanographene and aromatic architectures featuring π-radicals have attracted widespread research interest in recent years. However, the role of delocalized π-electrons in governing the reactivity and regioselectivity of radical-involving reactions, such as cyclodehydrogenation, remains underexplored. In this manuscript, we investigated on-surface reactions of tricyclo(dimethoxy-vinyl-phenanthrene) on Au(111). Following multistep demethylation and cyclodehydrogenation, kekulene-hexaone (KeO) has been successfully synthesized. However, systematic scanning probe microscopy (SPM) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) revealed an overlap between the thermal reaction windows of the initial demethylation and the first cyclodehydrogenation reactions at a remarkably low temperature of 423 K. Complementary quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations elucidated a π-radical-assisted mechanism for this low-temperature reaction sequence. The selective first cyclodehydrogenation can be triggered by spin density overlap between two neighboring delocalized π-radicals within a particular demethylated configuration. This configuration-dependent activation provides a fundamental atomistic basis for understanding regioselectivity in on-surface chemistry. Beyond the reaction mechanism, we demonstrated a frustrated assembly of KeO molecules which indicated a tautomerization (C═O⇌C–O·) of ortho-benzoquinone units driven by π-electron resonance. We believe this versatile electronic capability opens a novel avenue for engineering carbon-based quantum materials with exotic correlated electronic states.

title: Copper‒Chloride Semiconductor Nanoclusters for High‐Efficiency Photocatalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Research on atomically precise copper nanoclusters is ongoing, with particular attention paid to cluster systems that possess novel structural motifs and distinctive properties. Herein, we report a binary copper–chloride semiconductor nanocluster, [Cu 40 Cl 12 (ClC 6 H 4 CH 2 S) 22 (PPh 3 ) 9 H 2 ] (denoted as Cu 40 Cl 12 , where ClC 6 H 4 CH 2 SH is 4‑chlorobenzyl mercaptan and PPh 3 is triphenylphosphine), which possesses a covalent framework constructed through copper–chloride bonds. The synthesis of Cu 40 Cl 12 benefits from immediate separation during assembly in poor solvents and this synthetic approach is applicable to the corresponding copper–bromide and copper–iodide analogues. As revealed by theoretical calculations, the μ 6 ‐coordinated chlorides significantly modulate the cluster electronic structure and contribute to the formation of the electron‐hole pairs in the photoexcitation process of the Cu 40 Cl 12 cluster. Ultrafast spectroscopic studies reveal that Cu 40 Cl 12 sustains longer‑lived charge‑separated states and exhibits superior charge separation efficiency upon photoexcitation compared to chloride‑free analogues. As a result, a Cu 40 Cl 12 /TiO 2 composite demonstrates a remarkable solar‑driven hydrogen evolution rate of ∼9000 µmol g −1 h −1 under simulated sunlight irradiation and with methanol serving as a sacrificial agent, outperforming TiO 2 composites incorporating conventional metal nanoclusters. This work not only highlights the potential of copper–chloride semiconductor nanoclusters for photochemical transformation, but also emphasizes the broader prospects of copper nanoclusters in advancing research in chemical and materials science.

title: Electronic Polarization Induced Coordination Directs Crystal Facet Engineering for Cryogenic Rechargeable Li||Cl 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling the crystallographic facet orientation of in situ deposited products in conversion‐type batteries remains a fundamental challenge, as conventional synthesis‐based strategies cannot be applied to phases that nucleate and grow electrochemically during cell operation. Here, taking rechargeable Li||Cl 2 batteries as a model system, we elucidate the complete AlCl 4 − ‐mediated catalytic cycle governing the LiCl‐to‐Cl 2 charging conversion and identify the intrinsic covalent rigidity of the Al─Cl bond as the rate‐determining factor. On this basis, we propose an electronic polarization induced coordination (EPIC) strategy in which an in situ‐assembled [AlCl 2 (BZA) 2 ] + coordination cation (BZA = benzamide) activates directional N─H···Cl hydrogen bonds that selectively weaken the Al─Cl bond and lower the catalytic energy barrier. This molecular‐level intervention simultaneously redirects LiCl crystal growth from passivating {100} cubes toward dispersed {111}‐faceted nanocrystals through adsorption‐induced surface‐energy inversion, and operando x‐ray diffraction identifies these nanocrystals as the preferentially cycled, highly reversible phase, establishing a complete causal chain from coordination chemistry through catalytic kinetics to crystal facet engineering via a single design element. Li||Cl 2 cells employing the EPIC electrolyte sustain over 2500 stable cycles at −40°C under 1 A g −1 , tolerate current densities up to 30 A g −1 , and deliver 6.06 Ah in a cylindrical cell (ER26500) at 25°C.

title: Engineering High‐Performance Flexible Electronics Through Scalable Manufacturing: Interplay of Materials, Processing, and Morphology
abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible electronics have garnered extensive attention in recent years considering their promising applications across diverse fields such as communications, energy, display, healthcare, and wearable devices. Unlike laboratory‐scale fabrication and integration, the transition of flexible electronics toward commercial applications demands scalable manufacturing that ensures high performance, large‐area reproducibility, high yield, and throughput. However, achieving scalable manufacturing while maintaining device performance remains challenging, as fabrication scale‐up often induces variations in material assembly, morphology evolution, and device integration, which may compromise functional reliability achieved at the laboratory scale. Generally, current flexible electronic devices can be divided into two categories: planar‐type and fiber‐type devices, representing two complementary platforms for realizing large‐scale and highly integrated systems. In this review, scalable fabrication strategies tailored for each category and the latest advances are systematically summarized. In particular, the interplay among material design, scalable processing, morphology evolution, and device integration is highlighted, with emphasis on strategies that preserve device performance during manufacturing scale‐up. Representative planar‐type and fiber‐type flexible electronic systems are further discussed to demonstrate how the synergistic optimization of material design and scalable manufacturing approaches enables high‐performance devices for diverse applications. Finally, we outline remaining challenges and future directions to inform future developments in scalable flexible electronics.

title: A Single‐COF Photocatalytic System for One‐Pot Oxygen Reduction Coupled Ammoximation of Cyclic Ketones
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic oxygen reduction over covalent organic frameworks (COFs) has been extensively studied for H 2 O 2 production, but the in situ utilization of oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) intermediates in chemical synthesis remains underexplored. Herein, two porphyrin‐based polyimide COFs, IMCOF‐1 and IMCOF‐2, are reported as photocatalysts for the one‐pot ORR‐coupled ammoximation of cyclic ketones using O 2 and NH 4 OAc. Under light irradiation, IMCOF‐1 achieves a cyclohexanone oxime formation rate of 18.55 mmol g −1 h −1 and is effective for several other cyclic ketones. Mechanistic investigations reveal that photoinduced electron transfer from the porphyrin units to the electron‐deficient imide moieties promotes charge separation and activates O 2 at the carbonyl sites. The resulting surface‐bound *OOH intermediates are proposed to participate in ammonia oxidation and subsequent NH 2 OH formation, which then condenses with cyclic ketones to yield the corresponding oximes. In contrast to stepwise systems that first accumulate H 2 O 2 before ammoximation, the present one‐pot strategy enables the in situ utilization of oxygen‐derived reactive intermediates without requiring substantial bulk H 2 O 2 pre‐accumulation, eliminating the need for H 2 O 2 isolation, storage, and transport, thereby improving safety and atom economy while maintaining high selectivity. This work demonstrates the potential of directly harnessing ORR‐derived intermediates for the light‐driven synthesis of value‐added nitrogen‐containing chemicals.

title: Geometry-Induced Construction of Sub-Stoichiometric 3D Covalent Organic Frameworks for SO2 Capture
abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (3D COFs) have emerged as a rapidly growing class of crystalline porous materials, yet reported structures adhere to the reticular chemistry paradigm of fully connected building blocks. Here, we report a geometry-induced construction strategy that enables the synthesis of sub-stoichiometric 3D COFs─JUC-748, JUC-749, and JUC-750─by deliberately combining building blocks with similar geometries but distinct connectivity. Their structures are determined by continuous rotation electron diffraction and powder X-ray diffraction, revealing that connectivity incompatibility enforces partial condensation and leaves unreacted aldehyde groups periodically arrayed along the pore walls. The frameworks exhibit Brunauer–Emmett–Teller surface areas up to 2836 m2 g–1, and the spatially ordered aldehyde modified pores create a highly favorable adsorption environment for SO2. Remarkably, JUC-748 achieves a SO2 uptake of 16.9 mmol g–1 at 298 K and 1 bar, representing one of the highest values reported for porous organic materials to date. This work establishes geometry-induced construction as a powerful and general strategy for creating intrinsically functionalized 3D COFs with ordered reactive sites, high porosity, and excellent adsorption performance

title: Self-Assembly Driven Modulation of Photocatalytic H2O2 Activity in Acridine-Based Derivatives
abstract: Abstract Self-assembly provides a powerful strategy for regulating the photophysical and photocatalytic properties of π-conjugated organic molecules through controlled intermolecular organization. Herein, we demonstrate that molecular aggregation can either suppress or activate photocatalysis, depending on the structural and solubility properties of the catalyst. Two organic photocatalysts, Acr-1 and Acr-2, with distinct affinities toward water, exhibit markedly different H2O2 generation behavior upon self-assembly. Hydrophilic Acr-1 efficiently produces H2O2 in aqueous 3-(N-morpholino)propanesulfonic acid (MOPS) solution in its monomeric state, whereas self-assembly suppresses its photocatalytic activity. In striking contrast, Acr-2, which is inactive in its monomeric state, becomes photocatalytically active upon self-assembly. Spectroscopic investigations indicate that aggregation in Acr-2 suppresses nonradiative deactivation pathways and promotes productive photochemical processes, thereby enabling H2O2 generation. The resulting supramolecular assemblies remain stable under continuous irradiation for up to 4 h while retaining their photocatalytic activity. Scavenger experiments combined with spectroscopic analyses further elucidate the involvement of reactive intermediates in H2O2 generation. These findings establish aggregation state as an important molecular parameter for regulating photocatalytic function and demonstrate that supramolecular self-assembly can be harnessed to switch and maintain solar-driven H2O2 generation in organic photocatalyst.

title: Mechanochemical Synthesis and Co‐Former–Controlled Assembly of Azobenzene Polycarboxylate Organic Salts: From Framework Node to Passive Guest in HOF‐Like Architectures
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen‐bonded organic salts are versatile supramolecular materials whose architecture can be tuned through co‐former selection. Here, we report two multicomponent crystals of the azobenzene polycarboxylic acid 4,4′‐(diazene‐1,2‐diyl)bis(3,5‐dicarboxybenzoic acid) ( DADIA ): one with imidazole ( DADIA:IMD2 ) and one with N ‐methylimidazole ( DADIA:MeIMD ). Both were prepared by mechanochemical grinding followed by recrystallization from methanol. In each case, proton transfer from the carboxylic acid groups to the imidazole nitrogen gives charge‐assisted N + –H···O − hydrogen bonds, so the materials are best described as organic salts. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction shows that DADIA:IMD2 crystallizes in a monoclinic ( C2/c ) and DADIA:MeIMD in a triclinic ( P‐1 ), both forming two‐dimensional HOF‐like architectures. In DADIA:IMD2 , protonated imidazole acts as an active network node, generating channels occupied by disordered solvent. In DADIA:MeIMD , the 2D sheet is stabilized by O–H···O bonding between DADIA host molecules, with protonated N ‐methylimidazole housed in the pores as a passive guest. The compounds were further characterized by 1 H NMR, FT‐IR, PXRD, and TGA. These results show how a single N ‐methyl substituent switches the co‐former between the network node and the guest, with implications for gas storage, separation, and drug delivery.

title: In Situ Tröger's Base Scaffold Reconstruction Enables Programmable Growth of Missing‐Linker Defective Zirconium Metal‐Organic Framework Single‐Crystals
abstract: ABSTRACT Defect engineering of metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) offers vast opportunities for the manipulation of their local structures and has led to extensive discoveries from fundamental knowledge to property evolution. In this context, Zr‐MOFs, known for their exceptional structural robustness and chemical stability, are at the forefront of this rapidly evolving field. However, the development of defect chemistry in Zr‐MOFs has so far been limited to only a few examples and is generally tailored at the micro or nanocrystalline scale. In this work, we report that the in situ Tröger's base (TB) scaffold reconstruction, which occurs under the modular conditions typical for Zr‐MOF crystallization, can yield linker defective Zr‐MOF single‐crystals with sizes exceeding 300 μm. We designed three carboxylate‐functionalized V‐shaped TB ligands carrying distinct substituent (H, Me, and F). Upon crystallization with Zr 4+ ions, the methanodiazocine nucleus undergoes strap elimination reactions to produce planar diamine moieties. This skeleton reconstruction, accompanied by pronounced geometry reformation, engenders substantial lattice strain during the crystal growth, which in turn drives linker elimination and generates missing‐linker defects. The missing‐linker defects within the single‐crystals were thoroughly validated through a combination of complementary techniques. We also demonstrate that the large single‐crystals exhibit higher missing‐linker defect density than the microcrystalline powders, presumably due to the greater internal stress accumulated in the former. Moreover, the large single‐crystals with higher density of Lewis acidic Zr sites exhibit enhanced reactivity than the microcrystalline powders in the heterogeneous degradation of glyphosate (GPh), producing benign N ‐formyl glycine as the major product.

title: The Next‐Generation Layered Hydroxide Electrocatalysts Based on High‐Entropy Strategy: Synthesis, Characterization, and Electrochemical Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐entropy layered hydroxides (HE‐LHs) with five or more metal elements have drawn great attention because of their unique properties and scalable synthesis. Equipped with a tunable interlayer of two‐dimensional infrastructure, considerable atomic diversity, and promising industrial applications. These HE‐LHs have significantly higher mixed entropy and more complicated multiorbital hybrid effects than conventional hydroxides, which allows them to gain a customizable catalytic microenvironment, ideal conductivity, and thermodynamic stability. Although the high‐entropy strategy has been widely discussed in alloy and oxide systems, its immense potential in layered hydroxides remains undervalued. This review provides a comprehensive summary of the latest progress of layered hydroxides modified with the high‐entropy strategy, from the synthetic methods to electrochemical applications. The versatile synthetic strategies, including hydrothermal reaction, solvothermal reaction, co‐precipitation, and electrodeposition methods, are summarized. Besides, a thorough discussion of characterization methods for analyzing the basic structure of HE‐LHs is given and their electrochemical performance is assessed. Ultimately, this review briefly outlines the application of HE‐LHs in fields of oxygen evolution reaction, hydrogen evolution reaction, organic‐molecular oxidation reaction, and supercapacitors. This review provides a reliable reference for synthesizing and evaluating HE‐LHs, thus highlighting the giant potential of HE‐LHs and prompting the next generation of layered hydroxides.

title: Massively parallel self-assembly of suspendable microcompartments for functional cell screening
abstract: Modern biology increasingly demands platforms that can compartmentalize and analyze single cells and cell-cell interactions at massive scale, yet existing compartmentalization strategies based on microfluidics suffer from critical limitations. Emerging lab-on-a-particle technologies such as nanovials enable anchored single cells or small groups of cells to be isolated and assayed in a fully suspendable and parallelized manner using standard instrumentation, although their open architectures can result in loss of growing or un-attached cells. Here, we introduce capped nanovials: self-assembling hydrogel compartments formed by docking spherical capping particles into bowl-shaped nanovials. We routinely achieve capping of >80% of all nanovials in a sample and >90% sorting yield by flow cytometry, making the capped nanovial system well-suited for preparing and running large-scale assays. Furthermore, we demonstrate stable clonal expansion of single mammalian, yeast, and bacterial cells; growth-based selections of >10,000 colonies; enhanced signal-to-noise in secretion assays; and high-purity selection of antibody-secreting cells based on activation of co-encapsulated T cell reporters (>30-fold signal, up to 100% selection purity). By combining the simplicity of a well plate with the functional precision of droplet microfluidics without requiring oil or custom instrumentation, capped nanovials realize accessible, high-throughput, and high-resolution experimentation.

title: Dynamic Non‐Covalent Interactions at Oxide–Organic Heterointerfaces Enable Simultaneous Dielectric Enhancement and Mechanical Reinforcement of Organic Photovoltaic Devices and Modules
abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible organic photovoltaics (OPVs) demand both high efficiency and mechanical robustness, yet rigid non‐fullerene acceptor blends commonly suffer from an efficiency–mechanics trade‐off. Here, trace Al 2 O 3 nanofillers are incorporated into the PM6:BTP‐eC9 active layer to simultaneously enhance dielectric screening, charge‐transport balance, and mechanical energy dissipation. The nanofillers raise the relative permittivity from 2.48 to 2.78, promote exciton dissociation, suppress bimolecular and trap‐assisted recombination, and improve charge‐transport balance, raising the power conversion efficiency (PCE) from 16.1% to 17.0% for flexible devices, while increasing that of the corresponding rigid devices from 19.4% to 20.3%. Variable‐temperature FT‐IR spectroscopy and multiscale simulations provide evidence for thermally responsive and partially reversible interactions between Al 2 O 3 surface hydroxyls and polar moieties in the photoactive matrix, which are consistent with hydrogen bonding. These interactions are proposed to enhance intermolecular cohesion, homogenize stress distribution, and suppress crack initiation and propagation, increasing the crack‐onset strain (COS) from 4.6% to 12.0% and nearly quadrupling toughness. The strategy translates to flexible devices retaining 87.3% of their initial efficiency after 2000 bending cycles, intrinsically stretchable devices retaining 79.0% after 200 cycles at 5% strain, and an 11.4%‐efficient flexible module with a 100 cm 2 footprint and 68 cm 2 effective active area.

title: Machine Learning-Driven Electrolyte Additive Discovery for Ultrafast Charging of Sodium Metal Batteries
abstract: Abstract Sodium metal batteries hold immense promise for large-scale, high-power storage systems, yet their fast charging is severely constrained by sluggish Na+ transport across unstable electrode–electrolyte interphases. Conventional fluorine-donating additives suffer from inefficient self-decomposition, inevitably generating resistive organic byproducts. Herein, we propose an active machine learning framework based on Gaussian process regression to develop an innovative additive-triggered anion decomposition pathway. Guided by iterative screening of key physicochemical descriptors, a trace-level (0.02 M) sodium chlorodifluoroacetate (NaCDFA) additive is successfully identified. Theoretical calculations combined with in situ characterizations reveal that the NaCDFA thermodynamically promotes the targeted and continuous decomposition of the PF6– anion, enabling the construction of robust and highly conductive NaF-rich interphases, which substantially reduces the Na+ migration barrier. Consequently, the Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cell achieves ultrastable cycling over 50,000 cycles at an extreme rate of 200 C. Furthermore, outstanding performance is retained under rigorous practical conditions, including high-mass-loading cathodes and limited sodium excess or anode-free architectures. This work establishes a cost-effective trace-level electrolyte additive strategy for engineering fast-charging interphases, and demonstrates the transformative potential of machine learning-guided materials discovery for advancing battery technology.

title: Closed- vs Open-Shell: Unlocking Doublet Emission in Persistent Phosphorus-Containing Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Radicals
abstract: Abstract Persistent organic radicals embedded in conjugated materials are extremely rare due to the scarcity of suitable structural motifs capable of stabilizing unpaired spins. Here, we present a phosphorus-incorporated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon scaffold, along with its respective chemically reduced open-shell relatives, that provides access to these radical species. Two strategically placed keto groups activate new conjugation pathways that, coupled with two phosphoryl moieties, gives rise to a strongly electron-accepting molecular architecture. The resulting radical species demonstrate persistence in THF up to a week and are remarkably stable in ethanol, a feature rarely observed for π-system radicals. Despite the presence of the keto groups in the framework, the P-based closed-shell compounds display intense fluorescence with quantum yields of up to 54%. More importantly, the corresponding radicals are also emissive, constituting the first isolated luminescent radicals in conjugated organophosphorus materials. Intriguingly, these species feature dual doublet emission at room temperature that occurs through two distinct radiative pathways: one following Kasha’s rule and the other constituting a rare anti-Kasha process.

title: Mg(II)/H-Bonding Catalyst Design for Asymmetric Amination–Protonation Reaction
abstract: Abstract Given the strong interaction between amine and ketone groups, which often act as catalyst–substrate partners via iminium ion catalysis, the catalytic asymmetric aza-conjugate addition of common cyclic amines to unsaturated enones has never been successfully achieved. This model reaction is inherently challenging due to both the self-racemization of the amino–ketone products and the autocatalysis arising from the amine–ketone interaction. Consequently, this most straightforward and efficient route to chiral γ-amino alcohols remains unrealized to date. Herein, through the rational design of a novel Mg(II)/H-bonding catalytic strategy based on newly developed trihydroxyl chiral ligands, we have successfully suppressed the self-activation pathway between amines and conjugated enones, thereby achieving the desired amination–protonation reaction with high enantioselectivities. This new catalytic system proves highly effective for the one-pot synthesis of diverse chiral γ-amino alcohols bearing tertiary or quaternary stereocenters. Mechanistic investigations, including the identification of the formed metal complex and the true catalytically active species, the study of key transition states, and the elucidation of the coordination details of the Mg(II)/H-bonding catalyst through DFT-optimized processes, support a plausible mechanism for the asymmetric amination–protonation process.

title: Conjugation‐Activity Regulated Molecular Templates Enable Microcrystallite‐Refined Hard Carbon for High‐Performance Sodium Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT The microcrystallite structure of carbon materials has a significant impact on their electrochemical properties, yet it usually suffers from uncontrollable aromatic ordering and thickening during carbonization. Here, we develop a conjugation‐activity regulated molecular template strategy to program the microcrystallite evolution of coal‐derived hard carbon toward sodium storage. By modulating conjugation capacity and bond–cleavage thresholds of aromatic N‐heterocycles, we propose a molecular template design principle: strong conjugation creates supplementary microcrystallite growth sites to alter aromatic domain evolution, while molecular activity controls the effective activation range for conjugation‐mediated reconstruction. N‐Phenylcarbazole, which integrates a sufficiently conjugated aromatic core with a locally labile N‐phenyl linkage, realizes this balance by enabling radical‐mediated precursor reconstruction during pre‐oxidation and constrained aromatic‐layer rearrangement during carbonization. The resulting hard carbon exhibits refined and dispersed turbostratic microcrystallites with enlarged interlayer spacing and regulated defects, retaining 250.3 mAh g −1 after 5600 cycles at 500 mA g −1 , corresponding to 83.6% capacity retention. This work establishes an activity‐window‐modulated conjugated‐molecule design principle for programming coal‐derived carbon microcrystallites.

title: Ferroionic‐Assisted, Charge‐Driven Polymorphic Phase Engineering for Multilevel Memristive Devices
abstract: ABSTRACT Memristive device operation can arise from diverse microscopic mechanisms, including charge polarization and trapping, magnetic ordering, ionic migration, and structural phase transitions. Among these, crystalline–crystalline phase transitions in polymorphic materials offer a unique platform for nonvolatile resistance modulation but are often hindered by large energy barriers and limited endurance. Here, we demonstrate a multimodal, charge‐driven phase modulation in an atomically thin polymorphic material, Mo 0.92 W 0.08 Te 2 , enabled by electrostatic coupling to a ferroionic substrate, CuInP 2 S 6 . The polymorphic channel exhibits reversible switching between semiconducting and metallic phases via electrostatically accumulated charges, reflecting the intrinsically low energy barrier between its competing polymorphs. Integration with the ferroionic substrate enables spatially localized, nonvolatile charge accumulation in the channel, which provides distinct, programmable phase‐control pathways under a two‐terminal bias configuration. The phase‐induced resistance modulation through field‐driven ionic processes is governed by the evolution of a phase‐dependent Schottky junction at the electrode–channel interface, yielding multiple, stable conductance states under pulsed electrical excitation. Leveraging these experimentally derived synaptic characteristics, we conducted an MNIST inference simulation with a convolutional neural network, achieving 98.45% accuracy. This ferroionic‐assisted phase‐engineering strategy offers new opportunities beyond traditional phase‐change devices for adaptive electronic and neuromorphic material platforms.

title: Coupling Plasma‐Synthesized N‐Doped Graphene With Ice Templated Porous Electrode for Enhanced Aluminum Battery Performance
abstract: ABSTRACT Rechargeable aluminum batteries are promising for next‐generation energy storage owing to the low cost and abundance of aluminum. Graphene is an attractive cathode due to its high surface area and electrical conductivity, but its performance is limited by difficult production and sheet aggregation, which restrict electrolyte accessibility and ion transport. This study employs a plasma‐enabled synthesis approach to produce both pristine graphene and nitrogen‐doped graphene (N‐graphene), followed by an ice templating strategy to directly construct a three‐dimensional porous N‐graphene electrode. The effects of nitrogen doping and porous electrode architecture are systematically investigated by comparing dense and porous electrodes. Nitrogen‐doping increases the specific capacity by ∼50%, from 36.24 to 54.4 mAh/g at a current density of 0.1 A/g. Furthermore, introducing porous structure provides an additional ∼20% improvement, achieving a capacity of 65.5 mAh/g under the same conditions. This enhanced performance of porous electrode is attributed to its interconnected pores and partially aligned graphene sheets, which improve electrolyte accessibility and facilitate the adsorption and transport of AlCl 4 − anions. The robust porous structure of N‐graphene ensures excellent cycling stability, with no noticeable capacity decay over 5000 cycles. Coupling nitrogen doping with porous electrode architecture provides an effective strategy to enhance graphene‐based aluminum batteries.

title: Melting and resistivity of iron at Earth core conditions using pulsed Joule heating
abstract: The melting temperature and electrical resistivity of iron at high pressure are essential for understanding Earth’s core. Here we use a new high-pressure method – microsecond pulsed Joule heating in diamond anvil cells – to identify melting and measure resistivity of solid and liquid iron. More than 300 reproducible melting measurements indicate a surprisingly shallow melting curve, reaching 6 K/GPa and 4160 ± 80 K at 200 GPa. Extrapolating in pressure and iron alloy composition, and combining with our 76 μ Ω cm measurement of liquid iron’s resistivity, we infer a relatively cold core-mantle boundary (3430 K) with a low adiabatic outer core heat flow (9.8 TW). This suggests thermal convection alone could have powered the geodynamo prior to inner core formation and that today’s lowermost mantle is fully solid.

title: Ambipolar Electrochemical Doping of CsPbBr 3 Nanocrystals
abstract: Abstract Electronic doping underpins many semiconductor applications but has remained elusive for lead halide perovskite nanocrystals because their high density and low formation energy of defects easily compensate introduced dopants. Here, we use electrochemical doping as a strategy to avoid doping compensation. Electrochemical injection of electrons or holes into the nanocrystal is compensated by surface-adsorbed electrolyte counterions, therefore not compromising crystal structure. We accomplished ambipolar (n- and p-type) doped CsPbBr3 nanocrystals with charge carrier concentrations ranging from intrinsic up to 4.8 × 1017 cm–3 (corresponding to 0.25 charges per nanocrystal). We show that electrochemical doping is reversible and stable at these free carrier concentrations. The extent of doping and stability are enabled by the use of lecithin, a zwitterionic ligand that strongly binds to the surface of the CsPbBr3 nanocrystals while still allowing ion and electron transfer. Lecithin stabilizes the surface atoms by shifting the potentials for Pb2+ reduction and Br– oxidation outside of the bandgap. The inferred surface-chemistry design rules for stable electrochemical doping can also serve as a guideline for developing CsPbBr3 nanocrystals stable under high free-carrier concentrations in optoelectronic devices, such as light-emitting diodes or electronically triggered quantum light sources.

title: Real‐Time Discrimination of Parallel Single‐Cell Exocytotic and Exosome Catecholamine Signaling by Multichannel Hollow Nanoelectrodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Chemical communication in single cells often involves multiple vesicle release pathways that can carry overlapping messenger molecules. However, existing methods cannot discriminate between these pathways simultaneously under matched conditions, making their intrinsic relationship difficult to resolve. Here we establish a multichannel hollow carbon nanoelectrode‐based strategy for real‐time discrimination of classical exocytosis and exosome‐associated release. Distinct electrochemical signatures generated within the hollow geometry enable pathway resolution, while the multichannel architecture expands effective sampling coverage over the cell surface and improves event capture efficiency. Using this approach, we show that the two catecholamine signaling routes remain active under environmental perturbation but exhibit non‐compensatory changes in release activity. Under cargo‐loading disruption, classical exocytosis retains reduced catecholamine output, whereas exosome‐associated release persists but becomes largely chemically silent. These findings uncover a previously inaccessible chemically silent state of exosome‐associated release and reveal that cells can preserve a release pathway while selectively reshaping its chemical consequence. More broadly, this work shows that parallel release routes can convey fundamentally different chemical information under the same cellular conditions and establishes a general strategy for studying pathway‐specific chemical regulation in other secretory systems.

title: Addition–Migration Cascade for Ortho ‐Selective Carbon Functionalization of Phenols
abstract: ABSTRACT Ortho ‐ and para ‐carbon‐disubstituted phenols are prevalent in natural products and pharmaceuticals, yet their selective synthesis remains challenging. The strong resonance‐donating effect of the hydroxyl group renders phenols electron‐rich, activates both ortho and para positions, and limits their direct functionalization with external nucleophiles. Herein, we report an addition–migration–rearomatization strategy for the ortho ‐selective carbon functionalization of phenols using readily accessible para ‐quinol carbonates and diverse organometallic nucleophiles. The transformation proceeds through nucleophilic 1,2‐addition to the dienone carbonyl, followed by C1‐to‐C2 group migration and rearomatization, thereby enabling the formal installation of carbon nucleophilic substituents at the enone α‐position. A broad range of sp 3 ‐, sp 2 ‐, and sp ‐hybridized nucleophiles, including alkyl, vinyl, aryl, heteroaryl, polyaromatic, and alkynyl reagents, participate efficiently under mild conditions. DFT calculations identify syn ‐methyl facial attack as kinetically preferred over syn ‐Boc facial attack by 24.72 kcal mol − 1 , establish that both S N 2′ manifolds are noncompetitive, and show that aromatization proceeds via a Mg‐assisted decarboxylation/deprotonation pathway rather than an unassisted route. Synthetic utility is demonstrated through a concise five step synthesis of the bioactive natural product honokiol from commercially available allyl anisole.

title: Distinct PXR Inverse Agonism Mechanisms Rely on Differential Ligand‐induced Co‐Regulator Recruitment
abstract: ABSTRACT The pregnane X receptor (PXR) displays exceptional ligand promiscuity, yet the molecular basis of its antagonism remains poorly defined. PXR inhibition has traditionally been attributed to the displacement of coactivators from the activation function‐2 (AF‐2) surface. Here, we show that PXR antagonism is mechanistically heterogeneous, with distinct inhibitory mechanisms determined by ligand structure. Comparative analysis of imidazo[1,2‐a]pyridine, MI891, and SPA70 antagonists reveals multiple non‐canonical inhibitory mechanisms that decouple coregulator recruitment from transcriptional output. Notably, SPA70 preserves compatibility with coactivator recruitment while remaining transcriptionally inactive, consistent with concurrent corepressor engagement and a distinct coactivator‐compatible antagonist state. In contrast, MI891 stabilizes a PXR conformation that favors NCoR1 and SMRT binding and impairs nuclear translocation. MD simulations and mutagenesis reveal ligand‐specific perturbations of α12 and the α10/α11 region that underlie these effects. Together, these findings establish a ligand‐encoded framework for PXR antagonism that extends beyond the classical on/off switch model.

title: Evolution‐Inspired Multi‐Objective Bayesian Optimization for Protein Engineering
abstract: ABSTRACT Protein engineering requires efficient navigation of vast sequence spaces under limited evaluation budgets, especially when multiple properties must be optimized simultaneously. We developed evolution‐inspired multi‐objective Bayesian optimization (EvoMOBO), an active‐learning framework that integrates path‐dependent sequence generation, global candidate competition, and explicit multi‐objective optimization, enabling efficient prioritization of high‐value variants without exhaustive library enumeration. Compared with state‐of‐the‐art methods on complete steroid receptor DNA‐binding domain (DBD) and ParD3 antitoxin landscapes, EvoMOBO achieved greater target‐region enrichment while maintaining sequence diversity across two‐ and three‐objective tasks. In the DBD landscape, optimization guided by simulation‐derived geometric descriptors enriched variants with satisfactory experimental performance without experimental labels. Building on this validation, we applied EvoMOBO to two enzyme‐engineering tasks using mechanistic descriptors, with experiments reserved for final validation. For an old yellow enzyme from Geobacillus kaustophilus , probabilities of substrate binding and reaction preorganization guided optimization of a non‐native oxidative dehydrogenation, yielding a variant that increased substrate conversion from 17.5% to 95%. For a formate oxidase from Aspergillus oryzae , stability‐related descriptors identified aggregation‐resistant variants that nearly doubled diethyl phthalate degradation in a photoenzymatic cascade. Together, these results demonstrate robust multi‐objective optimization by EvoMOBO and show that mechanism‐derived descriptors can effectively guide protein engineering toward experimentally improved functions.

title: Each Atom and Electron Matters: A Continuous Gold Nanocluster Series
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving continuous atom‐by‐atom structural evolution and elucidating the associated quantum size effects in metal nanoclusters remain highly challenging, primarily due to the intrinsic thermodynamic preference for discrete magic‐number configurations. In this study, we present a synergistic ligand‐engineering strategy that combines dynamic ligand coordination with fluorine chemistry to break this preference. The use of weakly coordinating phosphine ligands facilitates adaptive ligand rearrangement during progressive core expansion, while fluorine‐induced noncovalent interactions establish a robust molecular and supramolecular spatial lock, thereby stabilizing cluster molecules and enhancing crystallization. Through this approach, we successfully isolated and structurally characterized an unprecedented continuous series of gold nanoclusters: Au 41 –Au 44 . Comprehensive experimental and computational structural and photophysical analyses reveal non‐monotonic geometric evolution and atom‐specific modulation of electronic structure, thereby providing direct evidence for the principle that “each atom and electron matters” in dictating cluster geometry and electronic structures. Collectively, this work fills the structural gap in medium‐sized, phosphine‐protected gold nanoclusters and provides a continuous cluster series that serves as an ideal model for probing quantum size effects at the atomic level.

title: Spin‐Correlated Wavelength–Intensity Dual Modulation in Organic Diradicals via Excited‐State Channel Engineering
abstract: ABSTRACT Luminescent diradicals translate open‐shell spin dynamics into optical readouts, yet their spin‐dependent responses have largely been confined to emission‐intensity changes, while concurrent wavelength modulation remains rare. Here, we introduce a through‐space charge‐transfer (TSCT) strategy in which appending a δ‐carboline donor to a carbazole‐bridged diradical preserves the native through‐bond charge‐transfer (TBCT) pathway while introducing a higher‐energy TSCT‐related emissive channel. At low temperature, δCbCz(TTM) 2 exhibits pronounced magnetoluminescence (MagLum) enhancement together with an approximately 31 nm field‐induced blue shift, while zero‐field warming from 4.5 to 20 K produces an approximately 25 nm blue shift. Temperature‐dependent MagLum measurements show that the additional spectral and intensity changes induced by the magnetic field are rapidly attenuated upon warming, supporting a common spin‐dependent mechanism. The structural analogue αCbCz(TTM) 2 exhibits a similar dual response with a smaller wavelength shift, highlighting the sensitivity of the response to donor topology. Time‐resolved spectroscopy, variable‐temperature EPR, and quantum–chemical calculations support a spin‐correlated photophysical model in which magnetic and thermal perturbations regulate spin‐dependent population redistribution, thereby modulating the relative contributions of TBCT‐ and TSCT‐related emissive channels and producing correlated changes in emission intensity and wavelength. This work establishes through‐space excited‐state channel engineering as a route for extending spin‐correlated luminescence beyond intensity‐only modulation.

title: Direct Synthesis and Electrochemical Deintercalation of Mg-Intercalated Graphullerite
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) carbon allotropes have unique properties, synthetic tunability, and potential applications across several fields including catalysis, energy storage, and electronics. One such allotrope is the recently discovered graphullerite, which results from the oxidation and deintercalation of the layered rhombohedral fullerene polymer (Mg4C60)∞. The current synthetic approach to (Mg4C60)∞ is limited by low yield, phase impurity, and small crystal size, all of which preclude a comprehensive investigation of the physical and electronic properties of bulk graphullerite and its 2D derivative, graphullerene. Here, we demonstrate two chemical vapor transport methods that produce rhombohedral (Mg4C60)∞ and tetragonal (Mg2C60)∞ as millimeter-sized single crystals with near-complete conversion. Our methods spatially separate the starting materials to circumvent both the thermal decomposition of (Mg4C60)∞ and the significant disparity in vapor pressure between C60 and Mg. We find that using Mg foil results in a near-complete conversion of C60 into a mixture of (Mg4C60)∞ and (Mg2C60)∞. Replacing the foil with Mg2Si produces phase-pure (Mg4C60)∞ with an isolated crystalline yield of 55 to 62%. This high-yielding, phase-pure synthesis enables us to investigate the electrochemical intercalation and deintercalation of Mg2+ into the lattice.

title: Asymmetric Total Syntheses of (+)-Asperterpenoids D and E with a Concurrent Synthesis of ent -(−)-Homoverrucosanol
abstract: Abstract The first asymmetric total syntheses of sesterterpenoids (+)-asperterpenoids D and E, together with a concurrent synthesis of diterpenoid ent-(−)-homoverrucosanol were achieved from (S)-limonene through a chiral-pool strategy featuring a common late-stage intermediate. title: Quantifying Hidden Metabolites in 31P NMR Spectra by Physics-Based Spectral Subtraction
abstract: Abstract NMR spectroscopy enables reliable quantification of the metabolites present in a biological sample. The number of metabolites that can be assessed from NMR spectra is often limited by the intrinsically high complexity of the spectra, arising from the large number of molecules paired with their complex spectral patterns. 31P NMR based metabolomics embraces a reduced yet broad view of the metabolism and significantly facilitates the interpretation of the spectra due to a lower number of signals and a larger chemical shift dispersion. However, full quantification of metabolites can still be hindered by the presence of crowded regions. Here we exploit the fact that NMR lineshapes can be simulated precisely from quantum mechanical calculations for disentangling these crowded regions. Iterative subtraction of accurately simulated and fitted spectra of metabolites presenting isolated signals from the experimental spectrum yields meaningful residuals, enabling assignment and quantification of completely hidden metabolites. This approach ended at a noise-level residual spectrum, granting the full quantification of the 31P NMR spectrum. We implemented this approach in MR-SHIFT, a program developed in this work for spin Hamiltonian simulations and spectral fitting, which was then applied to the fully automated analysis of 31P NMR spectra of mouse tissues.

title: Localized 4f Magnetism and Low-Lying 5d-Mediated Photoresponses in Layered TmI2
abstract: Abstract Divalent rare-earth solids with a 4fn+1 configuration provide access to electronic structures in which localized 4f states coexist with low-lying, structurally responsive 5d states, yet the combined magnetic, electrical, and optical manifestations of these states remain underexplored in extended Tm2+ compounds. Here, we investigate layered TmI2 as an extended Tm2+ solid and employ Cs4TmI6 with isolated TmI6 units and dilute SrI2:Tm2+ as targeted reference systems. Structural, spectroscopic, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopic measurements support Tm2+ as the dominant oxidation state, while electronic-structure calculations reveal narrow, localized, occupied Tm 4f-derived bands and low-lying Tm 5d-derived unoccupied states, with substantially greater 5d dispersion in TmI2 than in Cs4TmI6. Magnetic measurements establish localized 4f13 Kramers-ion behavior on the triangular Tm2+ lattice of TmI2, together with a small negative low-temperature Weiss temperature and no evidence of long-range magnetic ordering down to 2 K. Comparative luminescence, photothermal, and photocurrent measurements reveal distinct photoresponses across the three systems within a shared electronic-level framework encompassing 4f–5d and 4f–4f transitions. Relative to Cs4TmI6 and SrI2:Tm2+, TmI2 exhibits a lower-energy optical absorption onset, weaker photoluminescence, and a more pronounced light-induced current response despite its high electrical resistivity. Its wavelength-dependent photothermal response broadly follows the 4f–5d absorption profile. Together, these results establish layered TmI2 as a distinctive rare-earth platform that combines the 4f13 magnetic characteristics familiar from Yb3+ systems with low-energy 4f–5d excitations, expanding the scope for investigating rare-earth magnetic solids with optical excitation channels beyond 4f–4f transitions.

title: Cation-Effect-Driven Modulation of Interfacial Solvation Structures Enables Fast-Charging Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract Fast battery charging is limited by sluggish Li+ transport at the anode/electrolyte interface, which is governed by the interfacial solvation structure (ISS). However, negative polarization disfavors anion accumulation at the anode interface, hindering the formation of anion-rich ISS required for rapid Li+ transfer. Here, leveraging the cation effect in electrocatalysis, we propose a cation-mediated strategy to reshape the interfacial electric field and construct anion-rich ISS in commercial electrolytes. With benzyltriethylammonium serving as a model cationic regulator, we show that it accumulates near the polarized graphite surface and forms a cation layer that alters the local electric field. This cation-mediated interfacial regulation promotes PF6– accumulation at the interface, redirects early solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation toward anion-derived pathways, mitigates solvent decomposition, and accelerates Li+ desolvation and transport. As a result, graphite-based pouch cells deliver ∼88.2% state of charge within 6 min, maintain stable cycling for 2000 cycles with ∼71% capacity retention, and provide ∼218.2 Wh kg–1 with 10 min charging. Beyond LiPF6-based electrolytes, this cation effect also promotes reduction of the anions in other lithium-salt systems. This work bridges electrocatalytic cation effects and battery interfacial chemistry, offering a practical route to fast-charging lithium-ion batteries.
